$schema_note: Hand-curated record of what ForgePact's boss soul pieces (ForgePact#197) rely on, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/soul_piece_model.py never reads it; tests/test_soul_piece_model.py reads both, checks the shared `cases` against the model and its own transforms of ForgePact's code, and (ParityTests, where ForgePact is checked out) pins ForgePact/plugin/include/ForgePact/SoulPieceMod.hpp's constants, seeds, base, key base and icon, act table with boss rooms, room rules and verdict words to this file. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/soul-piece-spec.md; the game facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21 and § 18.4; the act of each room is hs-game-sdk/curated/room_acts.json. A `status` is one of `static_reading` (read from the compiled game and paraphrased, no script text), `inference` (follows from static readings, not read directly), `owner_named` (the owner's decision, not a reading), `our_code` (ForgePact's own choice), `measured` (a live session read it; `capture` names the session's capture, a local file the hub does not track), `unverified` (a plausible value no session has read) or `pending` (a live check of ForgePact#197 fills it). A `source` is `<path> § <section>`, the path relative to the hub root and the section text appearing in that file. `seed_base` + act is a piece's seed `a`; `reserved_seeds` are other ForgePact items' seeds a piece must never take. `base` is the game item a legacy bag piece (the first builds') is made of: the repository entry of that name in that category, resolved by name at run time, of that class, `c` and `j`. `key_base` is the key a key piece is made of (resolved the same way), with the step of `b` per act and the tolerance ForgePact recognises a piece within; `icon` is the display sprite ForgePact writes on every piece under that item info key, with its ground companion (both hs_game_sdk sprite names). `bag_stack` is the game's stack attempt a consumable's pickup reaches (an hs_game_sdk script name): the argument that carries the item, the class rule it applies before anything else and the classes that pass it, the most one stack holds, and the struct it returns with the field AddToInventory reads; ForgePact's merge branch on it is our code and is pinned through `cap`. `gem` is the Gem of Incarnation whose `droprate.base` G ForgePact reads at run time by repository name; `ratio` makes the piece's denominator D = max(1, floor(G x numerator / denominator)), 0 (no piece) for G unknown, zero or negative. `acts` is one row per act: the boss object its room is expected to bring out (an hs_game_sdk object name, with the SDK's index), the piece's name, the act's boss room (an hs_game_sdk room name, with the SDK's index) where a piece takes the player, `named` (false would make the act drop nothing and move nobody) and the row's evidence. `transfer` is how a piece moves the player there: the game scripts ForgePact calls by their hs_game_sdk names, in order (no portal object, no offset). `room_rules` are the name rules that refuse a room on top of the act table, each with the verdict word it gives. `drop_verdicts` and `use_verdicts` are the words, in the order ForgePact asks them; `force_overrides` the drop verdicts `soulpiece force on` may replace with `hit`. `cases` are shared inputs and their expected answer: `drop` (DecideDrop; `act` is the room's act, 0 for none) and `use` (DecideUse; `act` is the room's act, 0 for none, and a `transfer` case names the boss room it leads to) are ForgePact's; `stack` is the game's stack rule (soul_piece_model.stacks) for an item `picked` up beside a `held` one, each `{t: class, b, c, a: seed, o: count}` (`o` 1 when absent), where a `b` other than the base's 12 or the key base's 2 stands for any definition of that class, and a `b` or `c` with a fraction is a key piece's real value, compared within the runtime's epsilon. A roll is uniform in [0, 1). `open_questions` are the questions about the game the live procedures answer (and the ones no session can), each with the live check that answers it, its `answer` once a session ran it, and the model's HYPOTHESES key where it decides one.

base.source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.4 Using an item from the backpack
base.note: Live procedure 1 read class 11, b 12 on the owner's own Edible PAS Logo (crafted in the session); Live procedure 3's base-consumable read category 11's entry named consumable_edible_pas_logo at index 12. ForgePact resolves b by the name at run time, never by the index. Class 11 is outside the bag's stack classes, so a piece never stacks (Live procedure 3's piece-apart: five items, each o=1).

key_base.source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.3 Key items: the repository, the Key tab and stacking
key_base.note: The follow-up (2026-10-12): a key piece is class 12 with b = this key's index + act x act_step (2.1 for Act 1 .. 2.9 for Act 9 on index 2), c 0 and its act's seed. By static reading the stack compare takes two reals as equal within the math epsilon, and the repository lookup truncates b; the save writes reals through string(), which by the runtime's documentation (not read in this game, open question key_piece_survives_a_save) keeps two decimals. Measured in session by the follow-up's Live procedure 1 (forgepact-197-piece-icon-stack-live-1): a whole b merged into the real key (merge-control), while pieces of one act stacked and other acts and the real key stayed apart (frac-apart-key, frac-stack, frac-apart-act, and the same for c 0.05); its stop did not save the bag, so reload-frac-kept and reload-real-merges-real were not observed. Not shipped: the Key tab's right-click reaches the equip script, never the use (keyuse-route: not-reached), and the owner kept pieces in the bag; the core's key-piece functions stay as research. tolerance is how far ForgePact lets a piece's b (and its c from 0) sit from the exact value and still recognise it: wide enough for a two-decimal round trip, under half a step. Which key is our default (the workorder's open judgement, Bifröst because the owner holds it for the merge control); ForgePact resolves it by this name at run time, never by the index (measured 2 by #197's Live procedure 3, soulprobe base).

icon.note: ForgePact's dress writes the sprite, resolved by name with asset_get_index, under itemInfoStruct key "11" on every piece; the ground item looks up Pickup_ followed by the sprite's name (#158's static reading), and hs_game_sdk.sprites holds both names. Measured by the follow-up's Live procedure 1 (forgepact-197-piece-icon-stack-live-1, icon-route: bag-only): a built Gem of Incarnation carries Gem_Incarnation_spr under key "11" (gem-sprite); the bag and the Key tab draw a piece with the gem's icon (icon-keytab, icon-legacy-bag); on the ground a piece keeps its base's own pickup sprite, never ground_sprite and never the error sprite (icon-ground failed against ground_sprite); no tooltip draws an icon (icon-tooltip). The player build's pieces drew it in the bag (Live procedure 3, on-icon). After a reload a piece stack still drew the gem's icon with the research probe's icon off, while the plugin's own registration of the pieces was in place (Live procedure 4, reload-base), so whether key "11" is saved with a piece was not separated.

bag_stack.source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.3 Key items: the repository, the Key tab and stacking
bag_stack.note: The stack attempt a consumable's pickup reaches. It takes the item as its second argument and applies the IsStackable rule to it first (classes 12 to 15 only, after an item-info flag that can only refuse), giving up before it reads a grid or compares a field, so a class-11 piece never stacks whatever its b, c, seed or count; for a class that passes it merges only while the summed count stays at most the cap (static reading; the cap was not reached live). Every path returns the game's s_ItemOperation struct, and AddToInventory reads its success at each stack attempt. Measured by the follow-up's Live procedure 2 (forgepact-197-piece-icon-stack-live-2): with the merge off two pieces took two cells (bag-no-stack-control); with ForgePact's merge branch writing success, tabNumber, x and y into the game's result the pickup finished as for the game's own stack, no copy left (merge-stack, merge-no-duplicate), another act and a real logo stayed apart (merge-apart-act, merge-apart-real), the bag drew the count (stack-draw), and the confirm on a true PotionUse cleared the whole stack (stackuse-all); its stop did not save the bag (save-written failed). Live procedure 4 (forgepact-197-piece-icon-stack-live-4) saved it by closing the stash and read the counts in the file and after a relaunch (save-written, save-defs, reload-stack-kept); Live procedure 3 (forgepact-197-piece-icon-stack-live-3) measured the player build's stack, take-one and save. ForgePact's merge branch on this script (SoulPieceMod.hpp DecideMerge, kBagStackCap) is the mod's own code, not the game's.

transfer.argument: the boss room's index, resolved from its name with asset_get_index
transfer.when: the frame tick after PotionUse answered true for the piece
transfer.travel_source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.5 Portals and travel between rooms
transfer.reset_source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.6 Zone state and a boss room's return
transfer.note: The owner, after Live procedure 3: a direct transfer, no portal. NetworkRoomGoto(<boss room>) with the player as self took the player to Act_01_Boss and Act_02_Boss (goto-travel), where the room's Pentagram_Boss_obj brought out the boss; a Portal_obj whose portalZone record held the boss room took the player to the zone's ordinary next zone instead (portal-travel and portal-travel-2 failed). Before the travel, ZoneStateExists(<boss room>) is asked for the fresh count and ZoneStateResetSingle(<boss room>) drops the room's saved zone state whatever it answered. Measured in Live procedure 2 attempt 2, 2026-10-12: after Gurag was killed, a second piece's transfer ran the reset (transfers=2 fresh=1 cleared=1 with no zone-call-failed, on-reentry-reset) and Gurag came out again (on-reentry-boss). That a re-entry after a kill without the reset finds no boss is the owner's account, not established: no session re-entered that way (docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.6). Live procedure 4, 2026-10-12, logged ZoneStateExists, ZoneStateResetSingle and ZoneStateExists again on a transfer under x64dbg (dbg-zonestate-exists and dbg-zonestate-reset). Only the boss room's entry is touched, never the current room's: a use inside a boss room is refused. The call's own controls (our_code): ZoneStateExists is asked again after the reset (cleared counts a saved entry that is gone after it), a failed ZoneStateExists or ZoneStateResetSingle call is counted zone-call-failed and the transfer still goes ahead, and the status line asks ZoneStateExists for the room the player left (left, leftsaved), an ordinary zone just left being the positive control.

room_rules.note: A room drops pieces when RoomActIndex gives it an act and no rule refuses it; towns refuse first, then the boss-room rules. A use transfers from any room with an act, towns included, and is refused (the piece kept) in a room with no act and by the boss-room rules.

use_rules.action: right-click the piece in the backpack and confirm
use_rules.note: Every verdict but transfer is a refusal: PotionUse answers false and the game keeps the piece. On transfer PotionUse answers true and the game clears the piece's cell itself, as it does for the Edible PAS Logo (Live procedure 3's use-takes-one), and the next frame tick carries the transfer out. The base's own PotionUse is never called for a piece while ForgePact is installed (no-base-effect).
